source_name: CBCG — Statistički podaci: Platni promet section
why_relevant: Top-level statistics hub of CBCG; the payment-traffic branch sits alongside monetary, fiscal, external and capital-market statistics. Useful as the crawl root because deep payment-statistics URLs on this site change (a previously indexed /r/statistika/statisticki-podaci/platni-promet URL returned 404 on fetch).

source_name: CBCG — Kalendar objavljivanja statistike
why_relevant: Legally mandated advance release calendar (Law on Official Statistics) for the series CBCG is the official producer of, including payment traffic. Lets the collector schedule fetches on the exact publication dates instead of polling blindly.

source_name: CBCG — Izvještaj o radu CBCG (annual work report)
why_relevant: The CBCG states that the results of its payment-system oversight activity are published in the annual work report. That makes this the narrative and annual-aggregate counterpart to the monthly volume series — participants, incidents, availability, oversight assessments, project milestones such as SEPA and TIPS-clone.

source_name: CBCG — Nadgledanje platnih sistema (payment system oversight function)
why_relevant: Describes the oversight mandate, the systems under oversight and where oversight results are published; the natural pointer to designated systems, oversight standards applied and any dedicated oversight reports.

source_name: CBCG — RTGS sistem (system description page)
why_relevant: Defines the RTGS leg: gross real-time settlement between participants, the regulatory minimum transaction value that forces a payment into RTGS, operating hours and participant list. Needed to interpret the RTGS/DNS split correctly rather than mis-reading it as a retail/wholesale split.

source_name: CBCG — DNS sistem (deferred net settlement description)
why_relevant: The retail/low-value leg of the national payment system — carries roughly 60% of order volume but under 6% of value. Essential for any retail-payments or cash-substitution analysis.

source_name: CBCG — Podaci o realizovanom platnom prometu: RTGS i DNS sistem
why_relevant: The recurring monthly release of realised payment traffic (working days, total orders, total value, RTGS/DNS shares, daily averages). This is the page whose numbers are recycled by the Montenegrin press each month, so it is the upstream primary for those stories.

source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata
why_relevant: Licensed e-money institutions — the reporting population behind the e-money half of the quarterly payments dataset and an early indicator of fintech entry into the Montenegrin market.

source_name: CBCG — Centralni registar transakcionih računa pravnih lica i preduzetnika (CRTR)
why_relevant: Central register of business transaction accounts, including blocked-account data. An indirect but high-frequency indicator of account penetration, banking-relationship concentration and payment-system stress in the corporate segment.

source_name: CBCG — Podzakonski akti: Platni promet i platni sistemi (incl. Odluka o izvještajima)
why_relevant: The secondary legislation that defines exactly which payment statistics must be reported, in which template and at what frequency (the Odluka o izvještajima koji se dostavljaju CBCG o platnom prometu, amended in Sl. list CG 82/17, 107/20, 10/26, 47/26 per search results). Reading the reporting forms tells you which fields exist before the aggregates are published, and amendments forewarn breaks in the series.

source_name: European Payments Council — Registers of Participants in SEPA payment schemes (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD)
why_relevant: The definitive scheme-by-scheme list of adhering PSPs. Because Montenegro entered the SEPA geographical scope with an Operational Readiness Date of 5 October 2025, counting Montenegrin BICs appearing in the SCT, SCT Inst and SDD registers over time is the cleanest measurable proxy for SEPA migration depth — a series the CBCG does not publish as such.

source_name: CBCG press releases / Odnosi s javnošću (SEPA and IPS announcements)
why_relevant: CBCG press releases carry the milestone dates and first-load numbers that never reach the statistical tables — SEPA geographical-scope entry (6 October 2025), the EPC licence for the TIPS-clone, the 20 July 2026 IPS go-live with all 11 banks participating from day one, and early instant-payment uptake claims.

source_name: BIS Central Bankers' Speeches — CBCG governor/vice-governor speeches on instant payments
why_relevant: CBCG leadership speeches archived by BIS give quantified, forward-looking statements about the instant-payment rollout, fraud/AML controls and volumes that predate the statistical releases. An example is the speech at the regional conference on AML/CFT and anti-fraud procedures for instant payments.

source_name: World Bank / IMF FSAP Montenegro — Technical Note on Financial Infrastructure
why_relevant: Independent structural assessment of the Montenegrin payment infrastructure: the RTGS/DNS design, the EUR 1,000 threshold rule, the interoperable ATM/POS network routed through international card schemes, and the dominance of cash in retail payments. Gives the analytical frame the CBCG tables lack, though the vintage means the IPS/SEPA developments are not covered.

source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — Montenegro
why_relevant: Annual, internationally comparable series for ATMs and POS terminals per 100,000 adults and per 1,000 km2, plus account and transaction indicators, reported by CBCG to the IMF. Value is comparability with Serbia, Albania, North Macedonia and Bosnia, which the national tables do not offer.

source_name: World Bank Data — ATMs per 100,000 adults, Montenegro (FB.ATM.TOTL.P5)
why_relevant: Machine-friendly mirror of the FAS ATM density series with a clean API, useful as a low-effort long back-run and cross-check on the CBCG terminal counts.

source_name: MINA / CdM / Antena M / Aktuelno — Montenegrin business press relaying monthly CBCG payment-traffic releases
why_relevant: These outlets republish the CBCG monthly payment-traffic figures within days, in a consistent sentence template. Useful as a redundancy channel when the CBCG page is restructured or a monthly release is missed, and as a timestamped record of what was published when.

source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin banking and payments trade portal
why_relevant: Specialist local banking portal covering SEPA accession mechanics, the National Adherence Support Organisation (NASO) role, and instant-payment rollout commentary. Reveals institutional actors (NASO) that do not surface in central bank statistics pages and is a good snowball source for further actors.

source_name: Adria TV / Preduzetnica — instant-payment uptake reporting (CBCG statements)
why_relevant: Carries CBCG-sourced claims about instant-payment adoption dynamics (reported five-fold growth in transaction counts and changing consumer habits) at a granularity earlier than the quarterly tables. Treat the figures as attributed claims to be confirmed against the IPS statistics page.

source_name: EU Delegation to Montenegro (EEAS) — SEPA operational-membership communications
why_relevant: EU-side confirmation and framing of Montenegro's operational entry into SEPA, published in Montenegrin. Useful for dating the milestone independently of CBCG and for linking payments integration to the accession agenda, which drives future reporting obligations.

source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka and Tarife pružalaca platnih usluga (bank register and payment tariffs)
why_relevant: The 11-bank population that constitutes the RTGS/DNS/IPS participant set, plus the comparative tariff tables for payment services. Tariffs are the price dimension of the payments market and are published under a CBCG transparency obligation, which is rare and valuable.

source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin banking/finance business portal
why_relevant: Montenegro's only dedicated banking/finance portal. Publishes its own sector analyses (e.g. bank and insurance sector performance reviews), reproduces CBCG press releases, and runs card/ATM explainer and product content. Frequently the first local carrier of card-business and ATM-network figures quoted from bank executives.

source_name: Bankar.me — bank branch & ATM locator page
why_relevant: A media-maintained directory pointing to every Montenegrin bank's branch and ATM location pages. Useful as a pointer/actor map for ATM-network footprint work rather than as a statistics source itself.
